title: The Cartographer of Wrong Turns
synopsis: You draw maps of the roads that only appear when someone is truly lost. Past midnight, a soaked courier pounds on your door, begging for the way to a home that no longer has one.

nodes.text: It is the only trade you know: you map the roads that exist solely for the lost, the ones that vanish the moment a driver knows where they are again. Past midnight a courier hammers your door, rain-soaked and wild-eyed. "Six hours," they gasp. "I've been driving the same mile for six hours. Draw me the way out."

choices.text: Ask where they were trying to go
choices.consequence: You ask where they were trying to go. The path to The Address That Moved opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Just start drawing what they describe
choices.consequence: You commit to just start drawing what they describe. It carries you toward Ink Finds the Road, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: They give you an address, and your pen stops before it touches the paper. You know that street. That house burned down years ago; the family scattered; the lot is grass now. The courier is driving, at three in the morning, toward a home that is no longer anywhere on the map.

choices.consequence: You commit to tell them the truth, gently. It carries you toward After the Truth, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Map the road anyway, to the house as it was
choices.consequence: You choose to map the road anyway, to the house as it was. By The Road That Remembers, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: You dip the pen and begin. The paper resists — a dry stubbornness, like it does not want to admit the road exists — and then it yields all at once, and a route unspools across it that you have never seen, never surveyed, and somehow recognize the way you recognize a voice from another room.

choices.text: Ride along and follow your own map
choices.consequence: You ride along and follow your own map. The path to Two on a Wrong Turn opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Send them off alone with it
choices.consequence: You send them off alone with it. The path to The Courier Drives On opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: You tell them. They go very still, and then they weep — not surprised, exactly, more like someone finally allowed to. When they can speak again, they ask for something else. "Then don't map me the place," they say. "Map me the road to the person. They moved.

choices.text: Map the road to a person, not a place
choices.consequence: You commit to map the road to a person, not a place. It carries you toward The Road That Remembers, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Refuse — some roads shouldn't be drawn
choices.consequence: You commit to refuse — some roads shouldn't be drawn. It carries you toward Some Roads Stay Unmapped, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: You draw it, and this route runs the wrong way down time. It curves back through a lit kitchen window, a year that has already ended, a door that was painted over. It is beautiful and it is a wound. The courier stares at the paper like a drowning person watching the far bank.

choices.text: Let them take the road that remembers
choices.consequence: You choose to let them take the road that remembers. By A Window Still Lit, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.text: Take the pen back before it's finished
choices.consequence: You take the pen back before it's finished. The path to Some Roads Stay Unmapped opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: You climb into the passenger seat. The road you drew unspools past places lost by other people — a fairground that closed in someone's childhood, a bus stop where a promise was broken, mile after mile of everywhere anyone has ever failed to get to. Your map only shows the next turn, never the whole shape.

choices.text: Map every wrong turn you pass
choices.consequence: You map every wrong turn you pass. The path to The Atlas of Wrong Turns opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Get this one courier home and stop
choices.consequence: You choose to get this one courier home and stop. By The Courier Drives On, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: You press the finished map into their hands and step back into the rain. The taillights pull away, waver at the first impossible junction, choose it, and are gone — swallowed by a road that will erase itself the instant they stop being lost. The street is very quiet without them.

choices.consequence: You keep the copy you traced. The path to The Atlas of Wrong Turns opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Let it fade from the desk by morning
choices.consequence: You let it fade from the desk by morning. The path to Some Roads Stay Unmapped opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: You set the pen down and leave the paper blank. Not every lost thing wants finding; some people are driving toward a grief they are not ready to arrive at, and the kindest map is no map at all. You make tea instead, and listen to the rain, and let the road stay unmade.

The courier takes the road that remembers, toward the home that was and the window still burning in a year gone by. Whether they can stay there, whether anyone can stay in a place like that, is not yours to know. But they arrive. For one night, at least, they arrive.

You begin the great book: every road that only the lost can drive, bound in one volume at last. It will never be finished — new wrong turns open faster than you can ink them — but travelers start finding your door on their worst nights, and you are always, always up.
